conceptZh: 橡膠恐龍用短手怎麼也搬不動「口」，道具一直滑開，牠呆住的那一刻，口自己飄下來放在「木」上。
object: rubber dinosaur, a slippery mouth box and a tree shape
morph: 口 settles on top of 木
creativeAngle: 道具不聽話，主角放棄發呆時反而成功。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy, locked frontal camera. Setting: a pale-turquoise stage with a cream floor; the glyph is bold chocolate-brown 呆, a 口 square above a 木. A rubber dinosaur with huge feet and tiny arms stands at left, a loose box and a tree shape lie on the floor. The Traditional Chinese glyph 呆 stays centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): the dino squats and tries to scoop up the box with both tiny arms; it slides out and spins away; the first 呆 is spoken as the box slides. Moment two (1.8-3.5s): it chases the box, trips on its own feet and knocks the tree shape upright; the dino freezes mid-reach with a blank face, and the box floats lazily down onto the tree top with a soft click; the second 呆 is spoken at the click. Moment three (3.5-5.0s): the dino stares forward with half-closed eyes and its tiny arms hanging; a fluffy dust mote drifts past its nose and the dino does not react; 發呆 is spoken as the mote passes. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 呆 is perfectly still and unobstructed; the dino slowly blinks once, then slowly blinks again, tilts its head; the glyph is still. Audio: one warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in Taiwan-standard Mandarin, reading exactly these syllables with clear tones and no erhua: 「呆、呆、發呆」 (ㄉㄞ、ㄉㄞ、ㄈㄚ ㄉㄞ). Timing: first utterance at about 0.5s, second at about 2.6s, the word at about 4.4s; then stop, no repeats and no extra speech. Beneath the voice only soft thumps and one slide whistle, no music. The single glyph is the only on-screen text; the vocabulary stays audio-only with no subtitles, watermark, clutter or flashing.

conceptZh: 拉布拉多警長踮著腳偷拿豬探長看守的方形證物箱，豬探長突然醒來，兩人面對面大叫，警長滑過頭撞翻木架，木架疊成「木」、箱子落在上面變成「口」，兩人坐在地上一起發呆。
object: a square red evidence box (口) resting on a wooden stand made of one upright post, a crossbar and two slanted legs (木), guarded by a dozing detective pig
morph: the sheriff's panicked skid topples the stand; the post, crossbar and two legs clatter and re-stack as 木, and the flying red box drops squarely on top as 口, completing 呆
creativeAngle: 上一版是恐龍搬不動箱子的靜態呆住；這版改成「偷偷摸摸→被抓到→面對面尖叫→撞翻」的完整肢體笑料，警長「衝過頭」的個性直接成為撞出字形的動力，兩人最後一起呆坐把「發呆」演出來，聲音與畫面同步。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated slapstick clip, locked frontal camera, bright flat lighting. Setting: a pale butter-yellow stage with a soft mint floor and nothing in the background. The target Traditional Chinese glyph is 呆, a 口 square sitting on top of a 木, rendered in bold saturated navy-blue strokes; it must end centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with generous margins, and remain the only text on screen. Cast: the lead is a big friendly cartoon Labrador sheriff dog, golden fur, star badge on his chest and a whistle on a cord, eager and clumsy, who always charges in too fast. The one supporting character is a stout cartoon detective pig in a checked deerstalker hat, dozing upright on a little stool at right, snoring with a slow bobbing head, a giant magnifying glass drooping in his hoof. Center-right stands a wooden evidence stand: one upright post, a crossbar and two slanted legs, with a square red evidence box perched on top. Moment one, want it (0.0-1.5s): the sheriff pokes in from the left edge, eyes locked on the red box, licks his lips and rubs his paws together; the first 呆 is spoken at 0.8s as he lifts one hind leg into an exaggerated tiptoe. Moment two, the sneak (1.5-3.2s): he creeps across the floor with huge high knee-lift steps, each step giving a tiny rubber squeak; the pig snorts in his sleep at every squeak and the sheriff freezes in a wobbling one-leg pose, then creeps on; at 3.0s his paw is an inch from the box. Moment three, the surprise and the crash (3.2-4.8s): the pig's eyes snap open, nose to nose with the sheriff; both scream silently with wide-open mouths and flailing arms, cartoon tongues out; the pig leaps straight up onto his stool, the sheriff bolts sideways but his paws spin on the floor and he skids straight into the stand with a big squash-and-stretch BONK. The stand bursts apart: the post lands upright in the exact center, the crossbar drops across it, the two legs splay out beneath, re-stacking into a clean 木, and the red box arcs up, flips once and drops squarely on top as the 口; the second 呆 is spoken at 4.3s exactly as the box clicks into place and the glyph 呆 is complete. Moment four, the payoff (4.8-8.0s): the glyph 呆 is perfectly still, centered and unobstructed. The sheriff slides down to sit on the floor at the far left, the pig plops down on the far right, both well clear of the strokes, both staring blankly straight ahead with glassy eyes, mouths hanging open, little spiral stars circling above their heads; 發呆 is spoken at 5.3s exactly on this blank, frozen stare. At 6.5s the sheriff's whistle lets out one tiny toot by itself, he blinks slowly, gives a dizzy grin and a small proud thumbs-up without moving toward the glyph; the pig slowly tips his hat back over his eyes. The glyph never moves during the hold. Audio: one warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in Taiwan-standard Mandarin, reading exactly these syllables with clear tones and no erhua: 「呆、呆、發呆」 (ㄉㄞ、ㄉㄞ、ㄈㄚ ㄉㄞ). First utterance at about 0.8s, second at about 4.3s, the word at about 5.3s; then stop, no repeats and no extra speech or dialogue. Beneath the voice only soft rubber squeaks, one cartoon bonk, a wood clatter, a light click and the single tiny whistle toot, no music. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter, no flashing.
